name: A Killer Game Plays And Counts As A Killer (notes, mistakes, records, merge)
note: Written with the gate on 2026-10-01. Each mutation is a place where killer play meets code written for classic sudoku and could fall back to it.

mutations.name: a placed digit stays in the notes of its cage
mutations.why: The cage forbids the digit there as surely as the row does; leaving it in the notes is a pencil mark the game itself should have erased.
mutations.expectFailure: the cage forbids it there

mutations.name: a repeat inside the cage is not reported
mutations.why: A 5 placed where its cage already holds a 5 is told only "not the solution" — the one reason a killer player most needs to hear goes unsaid.
mutations.find: if ((cr !== r || cc !== c) && board[cr][cc] === num) {
mutations.expectFailure: not as a cage repeat

mutations.name: a cage past its sum is not reported
mutations.why: The sum is the killer's own rule; going past it is the mistake a player makes most, and it is reported as an unexplained wrong digit.
mutations.find: if (total > cage.sum || (filled === cage.cells.length && total !== cage.sum)) brokenSum = cage.sum;
mutations.expectFailure: not as past its sum

mutations.name: a killer win goes through the classic win path
mutations.why: Since 2026-10-07 one win path serves both kinds and the kind only picks the record (storage.js recordOf). Drop the kind from the call and a killer win lands in the classic record — the Logic Score's win rate and best times — while the killer card shows nothing.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer win must count in the killer record

mutations.name: every loss counts against the classic record
mutations.why: A killer lost or walked away from lowers the classic win rate — the number the Logic Score is built on.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer lost on mistakes must count as a killer played

mutations.name: the mistake handler forgets which puzzle was lost
mutations.why: The game over on a third mistake records a classic loss for a killer game.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer lost on mistakes must count as a killer played

mutations.name: a thrown-away killer counts as a classic loss
mutations.why: Starting a new game over a killer in progress takes from the classic record.
mutations.find: recordLoss(saved.variant);   // a thrown-away killer counts against the killer record only
mutations.expectFailure: counted in the killer record

mutations.name: "next game" after a killer is a classic game
mutations.why: The victory card's next game and the in-game new game call startNewGame with only a level; without the kind carried over, a killer player is dropped into classic sudoku.
mutations.expectFailure: "next game" after a killer must be a killer

mutations.name: a killer save without its solution is solved as a classic puzzle
mutations.why: A killer's givens fit thousands of grids; solving them classically picks one of them, and every right answer the player enters is marked wrong.
mutations.expectFailure: must get it back from its cages

mutations.name: the cloud merge keeps one phone's killer record whole
mutations.why: As an unknown field the killer record comes through from the local side only; a killer won on the other phone disappears the next time this one saves.
mutations.expectFailure: the other phone's 3 were lost

mutations.name: a speedrun's time goes into the plain table
mutations.why: Speedrun and plain games share one table-picking branch since 2026-10-07 (both kinds go through recordGameWin). Lose the speedrun branch and every speedrun time — penalties included — lands among plain times, for both kinds.
mutations.expectFailure: must set the killer speedrun Lv.2 best time

mutations.name: the win forgets it was a speedrun
mutations.why: The win path hands the record the mode; without it every killer speedrun is filed as a plain game.
mutations.expectFailure: must set the killer speedrun Lv.2 best time

mutations.name: the cloud merge keeps only the old killer fields
mutations.why: Until 2026-10-07 the killer record held games, wins and best times only, and the merge listed those. It holds every classic field now; a merge that lists the old few loses the other phone's speedrun times, flawless wins, combo and cleared levels.
mutations.replace: { const c = isObject(cloud.killer) ? cloud.killer : {}; const l = isObject(local.killer) ? local.killer : {}; merged.killer = { ...mergeGameCounts(c, l), bestTimes: mergeTimes(c.bestTimes, l.bestTimes) }; }
mutations.expectFailure: a killer flawless count only in the cloud comes back

mutations.name: the killer times fall back to the classic ones
mutations.why: speedrunRank picks the classic table for every kind: a killer is held to classic times and nearly always gets C.
mutations.expectFailure: must be S+ for a killer

mutations.name: the killer share line drops its grade
mutations.why: The killer line was written when a killer had no grade (before 2026-10-07). A language that loses {rank} shares a killer win without it, while every other language shows it.
mutations.expectFailure: the killer share line has no {rank}

mutations.name: the daily mission skips a killer win
mutations.why: Until 2026-10-07 a killer win ended before the mission check, so a killer player never completed a mission or got its hint. One guard is enough to bring that back.
mutations.expectFailure: mission undone

mutations.name: the Logic Score leaves the killer record out
mutations.why: The score counts both kinds since 2026-10-08 (one app, one score). Read only the classic record and a killer-only player stays at 100 forever, whatever they clear.
mutations.find: const k = stats.killer && typeof stats.killer === 'object' ? stats.killer : {};
mutations.expectFailure: a killer-only player scores differently

mutations.name: a killer time is measured against classic par
mutations.why: A killer takes ×1.8-3.2 the time of a classic at the same level (killerTimes.js); against classic par every killer best looks slow and drags the speed metric down.
mutations.expectFailure: killer times are measured against classic par

mutations.name: old best times stop counting as cleared levels
mutations.why: Saves from before clearedLevels existed mark a level cleared only by its best time. Drop that and those players' Logic Score falls — on the leaderboard, for no play of theirs.
mutations.expectFailure: classic-only records got a different Logic Score

mutations.name: a killer win does not send the Logic Score
mutations.why: The win moved the score; the leaderboard would keep the old one until a classic win.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer win sent the Logic Score 0 time(s)

mutations.name: a killer win records no ghost again
mutations.why: The guard that stood here until 2026-10-14 (killer order ④). With it back, Ghost and Time Gap on killer stay locked forever — there is never a killer run to race.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer win left no killer ghost

mutations.name: the ghost forgets which kind won
mutations.why: Without the kind the run lands in the classic slot: a classic player's Ghost chip offers a killer's time, and Ghost deals them a killer's givens as a classic board.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer win left no killer ghost

mutations.name: the win does not hand the ghost its cages
mutations.why: The ghost keeps a killer's givens without its cages; Ghost cannot deal that board again and falls back to a new puzzle, so the race is never on the board the record was set on.
mutations.expectFailure: the killer ghost must keep the cages it was won on

mutations.name: the cloud merge drops the killer ghosts
mutations.why: Saving uploads the merge: the first win after this loses every killer ghost from the cloud, and a restore on a new phone has none.
mutations.find: killer: { classic: ghosts(ck.classic, lk.classic), timeAttack: ghosts(ck.timeAttack, lk.timeAttack) },
mutations.expectFailure: a killer ghost only in the cloud was dropped by the merge

mutations.name: the cloud merge reads no killer ghosts from the cloud
mutations.why: A killer ghost set on the other phone never arrives here, and this phone's next save uploads the merge without it.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer ghost only in the cloud was dropped by the merge

mutations.name: the cloud merge ignores this phone's killer ghosts
mutations.why: A restore replaces this phone's killer ghosts with the cloud's: a record set here before the backup caught up is gone.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer ghost only on this phone survives the merge

mutations.name: a killer Survival game gets the classic limit
mutations.why: Killer Survival (KP-2, 2026-10-14). The limit stops being stretched by the killer ratio: 4 minutes for a killer Lv.1 that takes about 1.8 times a classic one, and almost every game is lost to the clock.
mutations.expectFailure: the killer Survival limits are

mutations.name: the Survival clock ignores the kind
mutations.why: The one place that chooses between the two limits picks classic for both: every killer Survival starts at 4/6/8/12/18 minutes.
mutations.expectFailure: the killer Survival limits are

mutations.name: a killer pays the classic 7 s a cell
mutations.why: The bonus agreed for killers is gone: a killer Lv.4 game, 38 minutes and 71 open cells, gains 7 s a cell and is far tighter than the classic one it is meant to match.
mutations.expectFailure: a right cell adds

mutations.name: the killer card reads no Survival best times
mutations.why: The stats card's killer Survival rows have no table to read for a player with no killer record yet, and the screen throws instead of showing --:--.
mutations.expectFailure: a record with no killer must still give the card its Survival rows

mutations.name: the killer card has no count of Survival clears
mutations.why: The card's Survival line is handed undefined for a player with no killer Survival clear, not 0 — whatever the translation does with a missing number is what the player reads.
mutations.expectFailure: a count of Survival clears, 0

mutations.name: the Logic Score counts classic Survival clears only
mutations.why: A killer Survival clear is a Survival clear (user, 2026-10-07: the kinds differ in the puzzle only); left out, the endurance metric of a killer player never moves.
mutations.expectFailure: the Logic Score counts Survival clears of both kinds

mutations.name: the AI room is a classic whatever the lobby asked for
mutations.why: The player picks Killer in the AI lobby and is dealt a classic: the switch does nothing, and killer order ⑦ (KP-11) is undone without a word on screen.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer AI room at Lv.1 holds a classic puzzle

mutations.name: the AI room drops its cages
mutations.why: A killer board without its cages is a page of givens — often none — with nothing to solve it by; the board draws no outlines and every digit is checked against a solution the player cannot reach.
mutations.expectFailure: has no playable cages

mutations.name: the AI room deals only its board and solution again
mutations.why: The hand-off before KP-11: the room is a killer, the game is not — no cages drawn, notes not cleared by cage, mistakes not told about cages, the win in the classic record.
mutations.find: return { board: room.puzzle, solution: room.solution, variant: variantOf(room), cages: room.cages || null };
mutations.expectFailure: handed only its board, a killer is played as a classic

mutations.name: the dealt game keeps the kind but loses the cages
mutations.why: The game knows it is a killer and has no cages: nothing to draw, and the solution is worked out again from nothing.
mutations.find: return { board: room.puzzle, solution: room.solution, variant: variantOf(room), cages: room.cages || null };
mutations.replace: return { board: room.puzzle, solution: room.solution, variant: variantOf(room), cages: null };
mutations.expectFailure: does not carry the room's cages

mutations.name: the killer bot runs at the classic pace
mutations.why: A killer takes 1.77-3.19 times as long as a classic at the same level (killerTimes.js); at the classic pace the Lv.3 bot finishes a killer in 2m 40s, and nobody beats it.
mutations.expectFailure: the killer bot at Lv.1 takes a step every 9000 ms

mutations.name: the bot match ignores the room it races
mutations.why: The killer pace exists and is never asked for: the room is a killer, the bot is started as a classic, and the player races a bot two to three times too fast.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer room raced at the classic pace

mutations.name: the bot drops the kind it is started with
mutations.why: Same race, one step further down: the session asks for a killer bot and the service plays the classic one.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer room raced at the classic pace

mutations.name: a duel won counts in the games played and won again
mutations.why: BT-1: a duel won came through the win path and a duel lost to a faster board did not, so every duel could raise the win rate — and with it the Logic Score on the leaderboard — and none could lower it. A killer duel must stay out as a classic one does.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer AI battle won counted

mutations.name: a duel lost on mistakes counts as a game played
mutations.why: The other half of BT-1: the duel record already counts the loss, and counting it here too lowers the killer win rate for a match the win path never counts.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer AI battle lost on mistakes counted
